title: Absolute frequency measurement of the $^{176}$Lu$^+\,(^{3}\mathrm{D}_1)$ standard against the NRC-FCs2 fountain with $2.6\times10^{-16}$ uncertainty
authors: K. J. Arnold, Bin Jian, Zhao Zhang, Qi Zhao, Qin Qichen, N. Jayjong, M. D. K. Lee, Scott Beattie, M. D. Barrett
abstract: We report an improved absolute frequency measurement of the $^{176}$Lu$^+\,(^{3}\mathrm{D}_1)$ optical frequency standard, evaluated via a remote link to the NRC-FCs2 caesium fountain primary frequency standard. Operating a single ion clock with 94.2% uptime over 10 days, and using an ambiguity-resolved precise point positioning (PPP-AR) link over the Global Positioning System (GPS), we determine an absolute frequency of $353\,638\,794\,073\,800.33(9)\,$Hz at a fractional uncertainty of $2.6 \times 10^{-16}$. This agrees with our previous result, which underpins the CIPM recommended frequency value, and reduces the uncertainty by a factor of 3.6.
summary: The research reports an improved measurement of the $^{176}	ext{Lu}^+$ ion clock frequency by linking it to the NRC-FCs2 caesium fountain standard via GPS timing signals. The authors achieved an unprecedented fractional uncertainty of $2.6 	imes 10^{-16}$, confirming its high accuracy and reducing previous uncertainties significantly.
main_problem: To perform an improved absolute frequency measurement of the highly precise $^{176}	ext{Lu}^+ (3	ext{D}_1)$ optical clock standard by linking it to the established NRC-FCs2 caesium fountain primary frequency standard.
main_result: The authors determined the absolute frequency of the Lu$^+$ standard to be $353,638,794,073,800.33(9)	ext{ Hz}$, achieving a fractional uncertainty of $2.6 	imes 10^{-16}$. This significantly improves previous measurements by a factor of 3.6.
method: The measurement utilized a remote link established via an ambiguity-resolved precise point positioning (PPP-AR) connection over GPS, comparing the ion clock to the caesium fountain standard over a 10-day period.
model_or_system: The experiment involves two primary atomic clocks: a single $^{176}	ext{Lu}^+$ ion trapped in a Paul trap and the NRC-FCs2 caesium fountain. The comparison is mediated by GPS timing links connecting local hydrogen masers to both standards.
key_observables: Absolute frequency of $^{176}	ext{Lu}^+ (3	ext{D}_1)$, frequency difference $y(	ext{Lu}^+ - 	ext{FCs2})$, and the overall fractional uncertainty ($\sigma/f$).
important_parameters: Fractional uncertainty limit of $2.6 	imes 10^{-16}$; comparison against the CIPM recommended value; systematic uncertainties from gravitational redshift and clock stability.
main_assumptions: The final measurement is limited by the instability of the NRC-FCs2 standard, which dominates the total systematic uncertainty budget.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate frequency offsets between various local oscillators (e.g., Lu$^+$ vs NUS HM) and noise models (Allan deviation), while tables detail the systematic uncertainty budget for the FCs2 standard.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup, including the ion clock interrogation technique (Hyper-Ramsey spectroscopy) and the link establishment via GPS PPP-AR. It then presents a detailed analysis of systematic uncertainties from both clocks before reporting the final frequency comparison and absolute value.
why_interesting: This work represents state-of-the-art optical atomic clock metrology, pushing the limits of timekeeping accuracy by comparing two different types of primary standards (ion vs. fountain) over a global link.
